name: Georgian three-voice polyphony
lineage: Georgian Caucasian three-voice unaccompanied polyphonic tradition — comprising four regional sub-traditions each with distinct three-voice configuration: Kakhetian table-song (two soloists carrying upper voices over a sustained choral drone bani, the eastern-Georgian wine-toast supra context), Gurian three-voice with krimanchuli (the western-Georgian high-yodeling M1-M2-alternation upper voice over mtkmeli lead and bani drone, the most contrapuntally complex regional style), Megrelian funeral lament (the western-coastal-Georgian three-voice with text-carrying mtkmeli), and Svanetian highland complex three-voice (the upper-mountain Svaneti regional style with archaic non-tempered fifth-and-fourth harmony); twentieth-century preservation through the Anchiskhati Choir Tbilisi, Rustavi Choir, the ethnomusicology lineage of Joseb Jordania, Edisher Garaqanidze, and the Tbilisi State Conservatoire folk-polyphony research program; performed in church-and-supra contexts using non-tempered Pythagorean-leaning fifths and fourths, the harmonic vocabulary distinct from Western tempered choral practice
